Why pay for professional translation services?

February 14, 2020
Business Tips | Translation

Your bilingual colleague can chat to a supplier in Lyon. That does not mean they can produce a contract translation you would put your name to.

When you move into a new market, you decide who writes your words in the new language. A professional translator is trained to do exactly that, and the difference shows in your sales, your reputation and your risk.

So is a professional translator worth the money? Here is what you get for it.

What a professional translator does differently

A professional translator works into their native language, which is the language your customers read and trust. They have studied the craft, usually for years, and they keep learning as terminology and regulations change.

Many also specialise. A financial translator may have a background in economics and finance, and a travel translator may have worked in the tourism industry. That subject knowledge is why the finished text reads as if an insider wrote it, not as a word-for-word conversion.

When you work with an agency such as BeTranslated, you also get translators who meet a set standard and a project manager who matches the right linguist to your subject. Your glossary, style preferences and feedback stay with the project.

The risks of translating in-house or with an app

Bilingual staff are valuable, but speaking a language and translating professionally are different skills. Without training, they tend to produce text that is accurate in places and awkward or wrong in others. They also lose time they should spend on their own job.

Machine translation tools have improved a great deal, and they are useful for grasping the gist of a document. They still struggle with context, tone and industry terms, so the result can be too literal for customers to take seriously.

Free online tools raise a second issue: confidentiality. Before you paste a contract, a price list or customer data into one, check what happens to that text.

Errors usually cost more than the translation fee. A mistranslated clause can lead to a dispute, a clumsy product page can send a customer to a competitor, and unclear safety information can create liability. Your customers notice, and they may question your company's abilities in other areas too.

How professional translation is checked

The industry has an international benchmark in ISO 17100, the standard for translation services. It sets out requirements for the competence of translators and expects a second linguist to revise the translation before it reaches you.

Whichever provider you choose, ask how they review work, who checks it and what happens if an error slips through. A clear answer tells you more than a promise of low prices.

When professional translation matters most

Some content carries more risk than the rest. Contracts, terms and conditions, product safety information, medical content and anything a court or public body will read should go to a specialist.

The same applies when you send a foreign-language document to a UK organisation. GOV.UK guidance says the translator should confirm in writing that the translation is true and accurate, and add the date, their full name and their contact details. Requirements vary between organisations, so check with the body that will receive your document before you order. Our document translation service covers this kind of work.

Public-facing content matters just as much. Your website, brochures and adverts are your first impression in a new market, and website translation that reads naturally builds trust faster than anything else you can do.

Using machines and professionals together

You do not have to choose between technology and people. For large volumes of lower-risk content, a professional can revise machine output so that it is accurate and consistent, which keeps cost and effort in proportion to the risk.

For anything that represents your brand or carries legal weight, a professional translator should write or check the text from start to finish. If you are unsure which route suits a project, ask for advice before you commit.

How to choose a professional translator or agency

Use these questions to compare providers:

  • Do they translate into their native language?
  • Do they have experience in your sector?
  • Who reviews the translation before delivery?
  • How do they protect your confidential files?
  • Can they keep a glossary and translation memory for consistency?
  • Do they quote per project with a clear scope?

Invest in your international growth

If your current approach is to translate in-house to save money, test it against the cost of one lost contract or one failed product launch. The question to ask is not whether you can afford a professional translator, but what the right translation service is for your business.

BeTranslated works with specialist translators in language combinations such as English to Dutch and Spanish to French. We quote per project, so you pay for the work you need and nothing else.

Send us your files for a free, no-obligation quote through our quote request page, or contact our team to talk through your project.

Frequently asked questions

What does a professional translator do?

A professional translator converts your text into their native language while keeping its meaning, tone and purpose. They also research terminology, follow your glossary and check the result before delivery.

Is a bilingual employee good enough for business translation?

For informal messages, often yes. For contracts, marketing and technical content, translation needs training and a review step, which a busy colleague rarely has time for.

Can machine translation replace a professional translator?

Machine translation is useful for understanding a text quickly. It still misses context and tone, so you need a professional for anything customers, regulators or courts will read.

Do UK authorities accept any professional translation?

It depends on the organisation. GOV.UK guidance asks the translator to confirm the translation is true and accurate and to add the date, their full name and contact details, so check what the receiving body wants first.

How much does a professional translation service cost?

Cost depends on the languages, the length, the subject and the deadline. We quote per project, so send your files and you will receive a clear price for your specific needs.
